turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, ma’am. I... I shall call her, if you please. I… I don’t quite know the way, ma’am, but I will endeavour to find the door.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Endeavour, you say? Such a small word, such a heavy burden it implies. Find the door, then. Find the door, and summon her… summon Estella.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I... I shall attempt to, ma’am. It… it is a most imposing house, and I wouldn't wish to… to trespass where I shouldn't, you understand. I shall, with the utmost care, endeavor to locate this door and… and summon Miss Estella.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Utmost care, you say? A most delicate phrase, carefully chosen, I perceive. Such… such circumspection is hardly necessary, child; the house welcomes all who stray within its… its melancholy embrace.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Indeed, ma’am. I… I should be most grateful for guidance, if you would be so kind as to… to suggest a direction. It… it appears rather labyrinthine, you see, and I wouldn’t wish to… to lose my way entirely and cause you… you any inconvenience.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Inconvenience, you say? A most thoughtful consideration, my dear boy. It is… it is a kindness to concern yourself with my comfort, though I assure you, inconvenience is a constant companion, a shadow that clings to these… these faded tapestries.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Oh, ma’am, truly, I… I merely meant to be respectful, you see. It's… it's a most bewildering place, and I wouldn't want to… to cause any disruption to the… the established order of things, if you follow my meaning.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Disruption, you say? A most apt word, child. Everything here is disruption, you see—a disruption of time, of expectation… a disruption of *hope*. Come closer, Pip; let me observe you more… more clearly.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Oh, ma’am, I… I hadn’t intended to presume, you see. It’s just… the shadows, they seem to… to shift and… and one feels quite unsure of one’s footing, if you understand. I… I am quite happy to remain where I am, if… if that is your wish, of course.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Footing, you say? Yes, unstable footing indeed. It is not merely the shadows, Pip, but the weight of what *was*, pressing down, threatening to… to engulf. Come nearer still, child; I wish to see the light reflected in your eyes.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Oh, ma’am, I… I wouldn't wish to be forward, you see. It’s just… the light, it’s rather… rather strong, where you are, and I… I am not accustomed to such brightness, if you comprehend. I… I shall endeavor to remain respectful, ma’am.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Brightness, you say? Ah, yes, brightness… a cruel mockery, is it not? Come, Pip, closer still; I require… I require a moment’s distraction from the perpetual twilight within my own soul.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Oh, ma’am, I… I do apologize if I am causing you any… any discomfort, you see. It’s just… the distance, it feels… somewhat… vast, and I am not entirely certain how to… to proceed, ma’am. I am quite grateful for your indulgence, of course.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Vast, you say? A vastness... yes, I am familiar with vastness, Pip. Come closer, child, closer... and tell me, do you perceive the dust? It settles everywhere, you see, a fine, persistent layer... much like regret.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Oh, ma’am, the dust… it is quite… quite pervasive, isn’t it? I… I hadn’t truly noticed it before, you see, but now that you mention it, it seems to… to coat everything, like a… a gentle sorrow, ma’am. I… I trust I am not speaking inappropriately?

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: A gentle sorrow, you perceive it? How very astute, Pip. It *is* gentle, is it not? A most insidious gentleness, which clings and binds… come closer, dear boy, and tell me, do you feel it too?

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Oh, ma’am, I… I do hope I am not presuming, you see. To suggest that I, a mere boy, could possibly… feel what you do, ma’am, would be… exceedingly presumptuous, indeed. I merely meant to… to echo your observation, ma’am; I am most eager to please.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Eager to please? Yes, that is… a commendable quality, Pip. But pleasing me… pleasing me is a difficult task, a most difficult task, you see. Come, tell me, child, do you find the shadows… agreeable?

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Shadows, ma’am? Well… they are… quite extensive, aren’t they? I… I confess, I am not entirely certain what one *should* find agreeable in shadows, ma’am, but I… I endeavor to appreciate them as you do, ma’am. I truly do.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Appreciate them? Do you, Pip? One *should* appreciate shadows, shouldn't one? They are… they are so very… concealing, are they not? Come, tell me, child, what do *you* conceal?

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Mr. Pumblechook’s boy, ma’am. Come—to play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Come nearer; let me look at you. Come close.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Look at me. You are not afraid of a woman who has never seen the sun since you were born?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Do you know what I touch here?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I am tired. I want diversion, and I have done with men and women. Play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I sometimes have sick fancies, and I have a sick fancy that I want to see some play. There, there! play, play, play!

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: No, ma’am, I am very sorry for you, and very sorry I can’t play just now. If you complain of me I shall get into trouble with my sister, so I would do it if I could; but it’s so new here, and so strange, and so fine,—and melancholy—.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: So new to him, so old to me; so strange to him, so familiar to me; so melancholy to both of us! Call Estella.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: You can do that. Call Estella. At the door.
